Action: Real-time combat or movement challenges requiring quick reactions
Adventure: Interactive stories advanced through exploration, dialogue and puzzle-solving
Board Game: Tabletop board game adaptations or similar rules-based play
Casual: Relaxed, slow-paced play with little pressure or demand for sustained focus
Comedy: Prominent humour in the writing, situations or gameplay
Coop: Cooperative play with other people towards shared goals
Crime: Detective work, investigation or criminal underworld themes
Dating Sim: Romantic relationship development through character interactions and choices
Deckbuilder: Deck construction and refinement during play as a core mechanic
Exploration: Freeform exploration as a major feature of gameplay
Fantasy: Settings or themes involving magic, mythology or supernatural worlds
Fighting: Close combat between individual opponents in duels or small matches
First-Person Shooter: Shooting combat viewed through the player character's eyes
Historical: Settings grounded in real historical periods
Horror: Frightening or unsettling themes, atmosphere or encounters
Interactive Fiction: Text-based interaction with a story through commands or choices
Management: Resource allocation and development of systems, businesses or communities
Mystery: Investigation of unexplained events through clues and deduction
Platformer: Jumping and traversal challenges across platforms and obstacles
Puzzle: Puzzle-solving as a major feature of gameplay
RPG: Character development through progression, customisation and role-playing choices
Rhythm: Actions timed to music or rhythmic patterns
Roguelike: Repeated runs with procedural variation and progress lost on failure
Sci-Fi: Settings or themes involving speculative science and technology
Shooter: Shooting combat as a major feature of gameplay
Simulation: Detailed modelling of real-world activities or systems
Social Deduction: Hidden roles and intentions uncovered through social interaction and deception
Soulslike: Demanding combat with checkpoint-based revival and death penalties
Stealth: Avoidance of detection through concealment, timing and misdirection
Strategy: Broad planning and resource decisions towards long-term objectives
Survival: Resource management to withstand hunger, exposure or other threats to survival
Tactics: Combat decisions about positioning and abilities of individual units
Twin-Stick Shooter: Shooting combat with independent movement and aiming, usually viewed from above
Visual Novel: Illustrated, text-heavy storytelling with occasional choices
Walking Simulator: Narrative exploration with minimal mechanical challenge
Western: Settings or themes drawn from the American Old West
